newsitem.title: JAPAN: BASKETBALL-NORTH KOREA LAUNCHES FIRST PRO TEAM.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL-NORTH KOREA LAUNCHES FIRST PRO TEAM.

text.p: North Korea has launched its first professional basketball team, christened the "The Typhoons" by the country's de facto leader Kim Jong-il, Japan's Radiopress news agency reported on Tuesday.
Radiopress said news of the team was reported in the August 5 edition of the Rodong Sinmun, the newspaper of the famine-hit Stalinist country's ruling Korean Workers' Party.
The article said the team, which belongs to the Yalu Athletics Association, was undergoing high-level training at the Yalu River Gym. The Yalu River is between North Korea and China.
"The team is conducting training twice as hard and twice as fast as any amateur team could stand," the Rodong Sinmun said.
The newspaper said basketball was a major area for development and that North Korea aimed to raise the standard of world basketball. "Playing basketball should be a major social movement," it said.
The article did not say if there were any other professional teams in the country or which teams they would play against.

North Korea's state-run media has recently run a series of articles on basketball. Last week, the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) reported that Kim Jong-il had instructed all North Korean basketball players to practice the long-range "three-point" shot.
The world's tallest basketball player, a 2.32-metre (7.61-feet) Ri Myong-hun, is a North Korean.
In May, North Korea denied rumours that the 27-year-old Ri, who was in Canada at the time, sought asylum so that he could play with a U.S. professional team.
